key_insight: The paper builds a transparent multi-agent LLM system to simulate coalition negotiations, while tracing every agreement clause back to party manifestos to measure influence and realism.
engineering_relevance: It provides a scalable, auditable framework for computational political science where model behavior, retrieval grounding, and provenance tracking can be evaluated separately.
method: SFT + DPO create partisan LLM agents with strong party-specific personas.
Per-party RAG constrains each agent to its official manifesto during negotiation.
MILT traces clause-level provenance, computes Coalition Influence Score (CIS), and compares simulated provisions with the real coalition agreement.
evidence_signal: Across three independent simulations, the system produced a stable winner and ranking (N-VA ahead of CD&V and Open Vld), and manifesto-anchored lineage predicted real-world adoption better than hallucinated content.
watch_item: The approach depends on high-quality manifesto retrieval and persona tuning; if grounding or alignment is imperfect, the provenance audit and negotiation realism can degrade.
paper_title: Digital Pantheon: Simulating and Auditing Coalition Formation with LLM Agents
